passages.text: This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him, and Abraham apportioned to him a tenth of everything. First, his name means “king of righteousness.” Then also, “king of Salem” means “king of peace.”
passages.sermon:
Melchizedek was king of Salem.
He was also priest of God Most High.
Melchizedek met Abraham.
Abraham was returning from defeating the kings.
Melchizedek blessed Abraham.
Abraham gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything he had.
The name Melchizedek means “king of righteousness.”
He was also called king of Salem.
King of Salem means “king of peace.”
passages.original: Οὗτος γὰρ ὁ Μελχισέδεκ βασιλεὺς Σαλήμ ἱερεὺς τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ Ὑψίστου ὁ συναντήσας Ἀβραὰμ ὑποστρέφοντι ἀπὸ τῆς κοπῆς τῶν βασιλέων καὶ εὐλογήσας αὐτόν ᾧ καὶ δεκάτην ἀπὸ πάντων ἐμέρισεν Ἀβραάμ πρῶτον μὲν ἑρμηνευόμενος Βασιλεὺς δικαιοσύνης ἔπειτα δὲ καὶ Βασιλεὺς Σαλήμ ὅ ἐστιν Βασιλεὺς εἰρήνης

passages.text: Without father or mother or genealogy, without beginning of days or end of life, like the Son of God, he remains a priest for all time.
passages.sermon:
Melchizedek was a priest of God Most High.
He had no father.
He had no mother.
He had no genealogy.
He had no beginning of days.
He had no end of life.
He is like the Son of God.
He remains a priest forever.
passages.original: ἀπάτωρ ἀμήτωρ ἀγενεαλόγητος μήτε ἀρχὴν ἡμερῶν μήτε ζωῆς τέλος ἔχων ἀφωμοιωμένος δὲ τῷ Υἱῷ τοῦ Θεοῦ μένει ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸ διηνεκές

passages.text: Consider how great Melchizedek was: Even the patriarch Abraham gave him a tenth of the plunder.
passages.sermon:
Melchizedek was a great man.
He was king of Salem.
He was priest of God Most High.
Abraham was the patriarch of Israel.
Abraham returned from defeating the kings.
Abraham gave Melchizedek a tenth of the plunder.
This shows how great Melchizedek was.
passages.original: Θεωρεῖτε δὲ πηλίκος οὗτος ᾧ καὶ δεκάτην Ἀβραὰμ ἔδωκεν ἐκ τῶν ἀκροθινίων ὁ πατριάρχης

passages.text: Now the law commands the sons of Levi who become priests to collect a tenth from the people—that is, from their brothers—though they too are descended from Abraham.
passages.sermon:
The sons of Levi become priests.
The law gives them a command.
They must collect a tenth from the people.
These people are their brothers.
The sons of Levi and their brothers all come from Abraham.
passages.original: καὶ οἱ μὲν ἐκ τῶν υἱῶν Λευὶ τὴν ἱερατείαν λαμβάνοντες ἐντολὴν ἔχουσιν ἀποδεκατοῦν τὸν λαὸν κατὰ τὸν νόμον τοῦτ’ ἔστιν τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτῶν καίπερ ἐξεληλυθότας ἐκ τῆς ὀσφύος Ἀβραάμ

passages.text: But Melchizedek, who did not trace his descent from Levi, collected a tenth from Abraham and blessed him who had the promises.
passages.sermon:
Melchizedek did not come from the family of Levi.
Melchizedek collected a tenth from Abraham.
Abraham had received the promises from God.
Melchizedek blessed Abraham.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ μὴ γενεαλογούμενος ἐξ αὐτῶν δεδεκάτωκεν Ἀβραάμ καὶ τὸν ἔχοντα τὰς ἐπαγγελίας εὐλόγηκεν

passages.text: And indisputably, the lesser is blessed by the greater.
passages.sermon: The greater person blesses the lesser person.\r\nNo one disputes this truth.\r\nThe greater always blesses the lesser.
passages.original: χωρὶς δὲ πάσης ἀντιλογίας τὸ ἔλαττον ὑπὸ τοῦ κρείττονος εὐλογεῖται

passages.text: In the case of the Levites, mortal men collect the tenth; but in the case of Melchizedek, it is affirmed that he lives on.
passages.sermon:
The Levites are priests from the tribe of Levi.
Mortal men from the tribe of Levi collect the tenth.
These men die.
Melchizedek is a priest who is not from the tribe of Levi.
It is affirmed that Melchizedek lives on.
Melchizedek receives the tenth as one who lives.
passages.original: Καὶ ὧδε μὲν δεκάτας ἀποθνῄσκοντες ἄνθρωποι λαμβάνουσιν ἐκεῖ δὲ μαρτυρούμενος ὅτι ζῇ

passages.text: And so to speak, Levi, who collects the tenth, paid the tenth through Abraham.
passages.sermon:
Levi was a descendant of Abraham.
Levi collected tithes from the people.
Abraham gave a tenth to Melchizedek.
Levi, in a sense, also gave a tenth through Abraham.
Levi paid the tenth because he was still in Abraham when Abraham met Melchizedek.
passages.original: καὶ ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν δι’ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Λευὶ ὁ δεκάτας λαμβάνων δεδεκάτωται

passages.text: For when Melchizedek met Abraham, Levi was still in the loin of his ancestor.
passages.sermon:
Levi was not yet born.
Levi was still inside his ancestor Abraham.
Melchizedek met Abraham at that time.
Levi was still in Abraham when this meeting happened.
passages.original: ἔτι γὰρ ἐν τῇ ὀσφύϊ τοῦ πατρὸς ἦν ὅτε συνήντησεν αὐτῷ Μελχισέδεκ

passages.text: Now if perfection could have been attained through the Levitical priesthood (for on this basis the people received the law), why was there still need for another priest to appear—one in the order of Melchizedek and not in the order of Aaron?
passages.sermon:
The Levitical priesthood gave the people the law.
The Levitical priesthood came from the tribe of Levi.
God gave the law to Israel through this priesthood.
If the Levitical priesthood could make people perfect, there would be no need for another priest.
But another priest did appear.
This priest came in the order of Melchizedek.
This priest did not come in the order of Aaron.
passages.original: Εἰ μὲν οὖν τελείωσις διὰ τῆς Λευιτικῆς ἱερωσύνης ἦν ὁ λαὸς γὰρ ἐπ’ αὐτῆς νενομοθέτηται τίς ἔτι χρεία κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ ἕτερον ἀνίστασθαι ἱερέα καὶ οὐ κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Ἀαρὼν λέγεσθαι

passages.text: For when the priesthood is changed, the law must be changed as well.
passages.sermon: The priesthood changes.\r\nThe law must also change.\r\nThis change is necessary.
passages.original: μετατιθεμένης γὰρ τῆς ἱερωσύνης ἐξ ἀνάγκης καὶ νόμου μετάθεσις γίνεται

passages.text: He of whom these things are said belonged to a different tribe, from which no one has ever served at the altar.
passages.sermon: Jesus is the one spoken of in these words.\r\nJesus belonged to a different tribe.\r\nNo one from this tribe has ever served at the altar.
passages.original: Ἐφ’ ὃν γὰρ λέγεται ταῦτα φυλῆς ἑτέρας μετέσχηκεν ἀφ’ ἧς οὐδεὶς προσέσχηκεν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ

passages.text: For it is clear that our Lord descended from Judah, a tribe as to which Moses said nothing about priests.
passages.sermon:
Our Lord is Jesus.
Jesus came from the tribe of Judah.
Moses never spoke about priests coming from Judah.
It is clear that Jesus did not come from a priestly tribe.
passages.original: πρόδηλον γὰρ ὅτι ἐξ Ἰούδα ἀνατέταλκεν ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν εἰς ἣν φυλὴν περὶ ἱερέων οὐδὲν Μωϋσῆς ἐλάλησεν

passages.text: And this point is even more clear if another priest like Melchizedek appears, one who has become a priest not by a law of succession, but by the power of an indestructible life.
passages.sermon:
The point becomes even more clear if another priest appears.
This priest is like Melchizedek.
This priest does not become a priest by a law of physical descent.
This priest becomes a priest by the power of an indestructible life.
passages.original: Καὶ περισσότερον ἔτι κατάδηλόν ἐστιν εἰ κατὰ τὴν ὁμοιότητα Μελχισέδεκ ἀνίσταται ἱερεὺς ἕτερος ὃς οὐ κατὰ νόμον ἐντολῆς σαρκίνης γέγονεν ἀλλὰ κατὰ δύναμιν ζωῆς ἀκαταλύτου

passages.text: For it is testified: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”
passages.sermon: God gives a testimony.\r\nHe says, “You are a priest forever.”\r\nYou are a priest in the order of Melchizedek.
passages.original: μαρτυρεῖται γὰρ ὅτι Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ

passages.text: So the former commandment is set aside because it was weak and useless (for the law made nothing perfect), and a better hope is introduced, by which we draw near to God.
passages.sermon:
God gave a commandment in the past.
This commandment was weak.
This commandment was useless.
The law did not make anything perfect.
God set aside this former commandment.
God introduced a better hope.
This better hope allows us to draw near to God.
passages.original: Ἀθέτησις μὲν γὰρ γίνεται προαγούσης ἐντολῆς διὰ τὸ αὐτῆς ἀσθενὲς καὶ ἀνωφελές οὐδὲν γὰρ ἐτελείωσεν ὁ νόμος ἐπεισαγωγὴ δὲ κρείττονος ἐλπίδος δι’ ἧς ἐγγίζομεν τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: And none of this happened without an oath. For others became priests without an oath, but Jesus became a priest with an oath by the One who said to Him: “The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind: ‘You are a priest forever.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
God made Jesus a priest forever.
God did this with an oath.
God said to Jesus, “You are a priest forever.”
God promised and will not change His mind.
Other priests became priests without an oath.
God made Jesus a priest with an oath.
passages.original: Καὶ καθ’ ὅσον οὐ χωρὶς ὁρκωμοσίας οἱ μὲν γὰρ χωρὶς ὁρκωμοσίας εἰσὶν ἱερεῖς γεγονότες ὁ δὲ μετὰ ὁρκωμοσίας διὰ τοῦ λέγοντος πρὸς αὐτόν Ὤμοσεν Κύριος καὶ οὐ μεταμεληθήσεται Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα

passages.text: Because of this oath, Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
God made an oath about Jesus.
Because of this oath, Jesus became the guarantee.
Jesus guarantees a better covenant.
passages.original: Κατὰ τοσοῦτο καὶ κρείττονος διαθήκης γέγονεν ἔγγυος Ἰησοῦς

passages.text: Now there have been many other priests, since death prevented them from continuing in office.
passages.sermon: Many men have become priests.\r\nDeath stopped these priests from continuing in their work.\r\nThey could not remain priests forever.
passages.original: Καὶ οἱ μὲν πλείονές εἰσιν γεγονότες ἱερεῖς διὰ τὸ θανάτῳ κωλύεσθαι παραμένειν

passages.text: But because Jesus lives forever, He has a permanent priesthood.
passages.sermon:
Jesus lives forever.
He never dies.
Because of this, His priesthood never ends.
His priesthood is permanent.
No one can take away His priesthood.
Jesus always remains the priest.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ διὰ τὸ μένειν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἀπαράβατον ἔχει τὴν ἱερωσύνην

passages.text: Therefore He is able to save completely those who draw near to God through Him, since He always lives to intercede for them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is our high priest.
Jesus lives forever.
Jesus always intercedes for people who come to God through Him.
Jesus can save completely everyone who draws near to God through Him.
passages.original: ὅθεν καὶ σῴζειν εἰς τὸ παντελὲς δύναται τοὺς προσερχομένους δι’ αὐτοῦ τῷ Θεῷ πάντοτε ζῶν εἰς τὸ ἐντυγχάνειν ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν

passages.text: Such a high priest truly befits us—One who is holy, innocent, undefiled, set apart from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is our high priest.
He is holy.
He is innocent.
He is undefiled.
He is set apart from sinners.
He is exalted above the heavens.
Such a high priest is right for us.
passages.original: Τοιοῦτος γὰρ ἡμῖν καὶ ἔπρεπεν ἀρχιερεύς ὅσιος ἄκακος ἀμίαντος κεχωρισμένος ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ ὑψηλότερος τῶν οὐρανῶν γενόμενος

passages.text: Unlike the other high priests, He does not need to offer daily sacrifices, first for His own sins and then for the sins of the people; He sacrificed for sin once for all when He offered up Himself.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is our high priest.
He is not like the other high priests.
Other high priests must offer sacrifices every day.
They offer sacrifices first for their own sins.
Then they offer sacrifices for the sins of the people.
Jesus does not need to do this every day.
Jesus offered Himself as a sacrifice.
He did this once for all.
He does not need to offer Himself again.
passages.original: ὃς οὐκ ἔχει καθ’ ἡμέραν ἀνάγκην ὥσπερ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς πρότερον ὑπὲρ τῶν ἰδίων ἁμαρτιῶν θυσίας ἀναφέρειν ἔπειτα τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ τοῦτο γὰρ ἐποίησεν ἐφάπαξ ἑαυτὸν ἀνενέγκας

passages.text: For the law appoints as high priests men who are weak; but the oath, which came after the law, appointed the Son, who has been made perfect forever.
passages.sermon:
The law appoints men to be high priests.
These men are weak.
The oath came after the law.
The oath appointed the Son.
The Son has been made perfect forever.
passages.original: ὁ νόμος γὰρ ἀνθρώπους καθίστησιν ἀρχιερεῖς ἔχοντας ἀσθένειαν ὁ λόγος δὲ τῆς ὁρκωμοσίας τῆς μετὰ τὸν νόμον Υἱόν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τετελειωμένον
